investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent 'BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 (+https://github.com/chriswatson6675/band_on_the_map)', no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official 'Programmation' page. This is a Nuxt (Vue) server-side-rendered application: every visible event card (a category tag, a French-language date+time string, a title, and an indicative 'from' price) is already fully rendered in the plain HTTP response, requiring no client-side JS execution to read.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.adidasarena.com/programmation immediately exposed dozens of fully-rendered `.app-programmation-card` event blocks, each with its own category, a French date+time string, a title, a price, and a detail-page link — everything this investigation's field_assessment needed. No escalation was required; Level 1 fully answered the investigation question.

venue_reference: Adidas Arena — 56 Boulevard Ney, 75018 Paris (multi-purpose arena, Porte de la Chapelle, Paris 18e)

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> reads 'adidas arena — Programmation' at the venue's own domain adidasarena.com, matching the well-known Porte de la Chapelle arena (the former Paris Arena / Palais Omnisports renamed). Every card image asset URL is self-hosted under adidasarena.directus.app (the venue's own Directus-backed asset store).

site_classification.platform: Nuxt (Vue) server-side-rendered custom application, backed by a Directus content store. Every visible event card is fully rendered as static markup in the plain HTTP response; no `window.__NUXT__`/payload.json client-hydration data was needed or found.

title.notes: Each card's own <h2 class="H2 bold"> text, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each card's own <h3 class="P2 date medium"> text (e.g. '28 AOÛT 2026 à 20h00'), a French day/full-month-name/year/time string, stated directly and unambiguously. One sampled card (M. Pokora) instead reads '2 & 3 OCTOBRE 2026' (a two-date run) — this project's own parser (ingestion/adidas-arena/observation-adapter.mjs) does NOT match this two-date shape against its single-date regex and honestly falls back to TEXT_ONLY certainty for that one record rather than guessing which date is meant; never fabricated.

time.notes: Embedded directly in the same date+time card text ('à 20h00'), stated directly. No timezone/offset is stated anywhere on the page, so this is recorded as a floating local time (Europe/Paris being the only plausible reading for a Paris venue's own listing), never upgraded to a confirmed UTC instant.

end.notes: No end date/time is shown anywhere on this list-card view.

venue_location.notes: The retained page's own <title> directly states the venue name; this is a single-venue source (every card is this one venue), so every Observation is resolved to it by source_id, not per-record text.

source_record_id.notes: This source exposes no separate numeric event id field on the card itself, but each card's own '/programmation/{slug}--{numeric-id}' href already embeds a numeric id as the trailing suffix of its own permanent permalink slug; the full slug (including that suffix) is used as source_record_id, following the same documented judgement already established for other sources in this project (a site's own URL-slug permalink as its stable identity).

event_url.notes: Each card's own href, stated directly, resolved against the venue's own domain.

price.notes: Each card's own 'À partir de {X}€' text, stated directly. Present on every one of the 7 sampled cards, including both music and non-music categories.

blockers.description: This one plain fetch returned dozens of event cards across multiple categories (concert, sport, mma, and others); whether this represents the venue's complete near-term calendar or a bounded/paginated subset was not exhaustively confirmed within this bounded investigation.

One sampled card's own date text spans two dates ('2 & 3 OCTOBRE 2026') rather than this source's usual single-date format; the parser correctly falls back to TEXT_ONLY rather than guessing, but a production collector may want dedicated handling for genuinely multi-date runs.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, self-hosted Directus asset domain).
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML, a resolved supported class, reached at Level 1 with no escalation needed.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: a single plain fetch exposing every currently-listed event card at once.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own URL-slug permalink, following documented precedent.

The card's own wrapper class directly states its category (e.g. 'concert'), giving this source a genuinely direct (not keyword-guessed) music-relevance filter — see ingestion/adidas-arena/discovery.mjs's filterMusicEventCards().

recommended_family STATIC_EVENT_LIST, requiring a small, genuinely bespoke card parser (no existing collector family in this repository already matches this exact markup) — see ingestion/adidas-arena/.
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker — both blockers are MINOR and documented.

evidence.description: The venue's official programmation page — the full raw response was 171,382 bytes, dominated by navigation/CSS/Nuxt-runtime markup carrying no event data on its own. This file retains the page's own <title> plus a contiguous run of real `.app-programmation-card` blocks verbatim (byte-for-byte substring), covering both music (concert) and non-music (sport, mma) categories as genuinely encountered, undisguised.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser); response then truncated to title + a contiguous run of .app-programmation-card blocks, disclosed in this description

evidence.description: A real, dependency-free, no-network offline test suite (tests/adidas-arena.test.mjs) re-parsing this investigation's own retained fixture (fixtures/adidas-arena-paris/programmation.html, a copy of ev-cards) via ingestion/adidas-arena/discovery.mjs + observation-adapter.mjs and reproducing the exact claimed field values deterministically (4/4 tests passing).
